ask: Set the PASS-004 test aside for now, or keep it blocking while we dig for the cause?
problem: One web test, PASS-004, fails about 1 run in 14. A pull request that did nothing wrong turns red and has to be run again.
found: I read both failing runs. They fail in different places: once the feedback step never appeared in 20 seconds, once the Record a fix button never appeared after a tap. The same test passed on the next run with the same code. Both runs were on a very busy test machine. The screen showed no clear sign of an app bug, but I could not run the full test stack here to prove it. So the cause is probably timing in the test or the machine, not proven.
changed: Nothing changes for people using the app. The test PASS-004 gets the quarantine tag, with this issue and an owner written beside it. It then runs alone in the nightly run instead of blocking pull requests.
why: The team's testing rules say a test that fails without an app cause gets set aside, never retried until it passes. I could not install the tools here, so I could not run any check, and I did not want to guess at a fix I cannot test. I also looked at the earlier fix for the same kind of problem (LAN-166); it is already in this code.
touches: Only the one test file. The nightly run will report this test separately.

pictures.label: A screen captured when the test failed (one of several devices in that run)

options.label: Set it aside now
options.result: Pull requests stop failing on this test. It keeps running every night, and the cause stays open.

options.label: Keep it blocking and dig deeper
options.result: About 1 pull request in 14 still fails on it until someone reproduces the problem with the full test stack.
